svg.text: Practical impact: who is affected, what is measured, and what is only intended
University GPU cluster, 100 GPU-hours, six teams. Official SDG icons; targets verified at sdgs.un.org/goals.
Mechanism: GPU-hours go to the group with the most project value net
of carbon, not to the earliest arrivals.
Demonstrated: computed on one synthetic instance
Resource-use efficiency and clean technology in
Mechanism: carbon enters each team’s score, so large jobs move to
the cleaner GPU pool when one exists.
Indicator: kg CO₂e per unit of allocated value
Demonstrated: computed on one synthetic instance
Mechanism: the institution publishes λ, issues a fixed credit
budget, and keeps a re-runnable allocation log.
Indicator: rounds with λ, credit supply, and log published in advance
Intended: requires an institution to adopt the rule

A heavy λ penalizes compute-heavy research (9.4 works against 9.5): above λ = 1.25 only two teams are
Publish λ before each round and cap it below 1.25, the bound found by the sweep.
The same low-value teams are excluded every round (VCG serves 4 teams; FCFS 4.93 on average).
History-based priority credits for repeatedly excluded teams (planned; Roadmap, CS study).
Adding credits mid-term removes their cost, and with it the reason to report truthfully.
Fixed credit supply per round (C2); no top-ups; spent credits are retired.
True values cannot be verified, and a misreport that wins a seat can displace an honest team.
Public, re-runnable audit log; a pilot comparing reported value with ex-post outcomes.
